name: Aconity3D GmbH
subcategory: research-grade, open-parameter laser powder-bed fusion (LPBF) machines; also DED (wire) and polymer SLS
origin_detail: LPBF machine builder based in Herzogenrath near Aachen (commercial register HRB 18970, Amtsgericht Aachen), managed by Yves Hagedorn (Managing Director), Andreas Goerres (Technical Director) and Hendrik Blom (Technology & Data Science Director); US subsidiary AconityUS, Inc. in El Paso, TX. Founding year, founders and any RWTH Aachen / Fraunhofer ILT spin-off origin could not be confirmed from fetched pages.
flagship_projects: AconityMIDI / MIDI+ (research LPBF with preheating up to 1,200 C / 1,000 C)
AconityMINI and AconityMICRO (small build volume for material development)
openness_notes: Scored 0 on the licensing scale because no design files, firmware or OSI-licensed software are published. But it is the most 'open' LPBF vendor in operational terms: its research systems are 'Open systems for everyone who wants to understand the process'; 'every parameter and scan strategy is freely accessible' with laser control 'layer by layer and vector by vector'; users get full access to process and monitoring data ('synchronised process data is available for analysis and publication'), open interfaces for third-party sensors, and 'documented interfaces' to raw data. The company's mission statement leads with 'openness'. This is open access to the process, not open-source hardware.

license_history.license: Proprietary machines and control software with open parameter and data access ('open machine philosophy')

robustness: Small private company with no disclosed funding, revenue or headcount; it appears stable (2026 product launches, a second user conference in May 2026, Formnext 2026, ISO 9001, America Makes membership, a US subsidiary in El Paso). Because users get full parameter and data access, the process knowledge generated on its machines stays with the user and is publishable, which reduces lock-in compared with recipe-based vendors even though the machines themselves are proprietary.
physical_science_relevance: The closest commercial match to an open-science LPBF alloy lab. Research configurations target 'new alloys and materials, superalloys and intermetallics, and graded or multi-material parts'; the AconityMINI research configuration shrinks the build to 55 mm diameter for 'material development with minimal powder'; MIDI/MIDI+ offer high-temperature preheating (up to 1,200 C / 1,000 C) for crack-prone alloys. Free access to every parameter, scan vector and synchronised sensor stream is what closed-loop or self-driving LPBF experiments (e.g. Bayesian optimisation of Al-alloy process windows) require. Listed users are mostly research institutions (ETH Zurich Inspire, IWT Bremen, UniBw Munich, FAU Erlangen-Nuernberg, Innsbruck, UTEP's W.M. Keck Center, TII). No aluminium-specific examples were given on the fetched pages.
openness_effect_assessment: Aconity3D built its niche on process openness rather than open licensing: by selling machines whose parameters, scan strategies and data are fully accessible, it serves universities and institutes that need to publish process data, a market the 'validated parameter set' incumbents (EOS, Velo3D) serve poorly. Without financial disclosures its commercial outcome cannot be quantified.
key_takeaway: Aconity3D shows a third path between open-source hardware and closed incumbents: proprietary machines sold as open research instruments, with every laser parameter and sensor stream exposed for analysis and publication. For a lab developing LPBF aluminium alloys and aiming for self-driving experiments, that open process access, not open CAD files, is the openness that matters, and it is a criterion to require when buying closed instruments.

firmware_software_licenses: Proprietary control software with open parameter access and documented data interfaces (licence terms not published)
